---
title: "1. Define a capsule"
subtitle: "The adopted v0.1 capsule contract: identity, capability, inputs/outputs, dependencies and versions."
---

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

- Name the required capsule-metadata fields and the contract
  boundaries a capsule declares (adopted upstream in
  [`memo1.md` §1](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo1.md#1-required-field-set-minimal)).
- Describe what a capsule declares about its inputs, outputs,
  configuration, dependencies and version at v0.1, and which of
  those fields are required versus optional (and why).
- Distinguish a capsule **contract** from any particular capsule
  **implementation**, and point at `spec.capability` as the binding
  surface a Pico resolves against.

These objectives map one-to-one to the three "Teach" bullets of
[`memo23.md`](../../../../memo23.md) §4 Module 2.

## Prerequisites

- Completed [Part 1 · Understand a Pico](../../part-1/01-introduction/index.qmd).
- A working shell and text editor.
- Comfort reading YAML.
- Python 3.8+ on `PATH` for the validator command referenced in the
  [Exercise](exercise.qmd) and [Lab](lab.qmd).

## What a capsule is

A **capsule** is a declarative contract for one capability. The
[adopted v0.1 contract](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo1.md)
is a `kind: Capsule` document with four groups of required fields
and a small set of optional fields. The normative schema lives at
[`capsule.schema.json`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/capsule.schema.json)
in `open-engineering-capsules/source` at commit `bf071c2c1b57`; the
accompanying [conformance fixture set](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/fixtures/README.md)
is the executable arbiter of what a conforming capsule looks like.

## Required and optional fields at v0.1

The table below is reproduced from
[memo1 §1](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo1.md#1-required-field-set-minimal)
at `bf071c2c1b57`. Required fields are the smallest set the course
Modules 2–4 cannot be taught without; every other field listed in
memo23 §3.2 is optional at v0.1 with a stated rationale.

| Required field | Role | Why required at v0.1 |
|---|---|---|
| `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata.name`, `metadata.version` | Identity and version | Module 2 cannot address a capsule or pin a version without them. |
| `spec.capability` | Capability name | Module 4 must bind a Pico's declared capability requirement to exactly one capsule by name. |
| `spec.inputs`, `spec.outputs` | Inputs and outputs | Module 3 tests a capsule against its contract; a contract with no inputs/outputs is not testable. |
| `spec.dependencies` | Capability dependencies | Module 4's dependency resolution and memo23 §5 rule 3 (Explicit dependencies) require declared dependencies; may be `[]`. |

Optional at v0.1 (each with a one-line rationale in memo1 §1):
`spec.purpose`, `spec.interfaces`, `spec.events`, `spec.config`,
`spec.secrets`, `spec.lifecycle`, `spec.compatibility`, `spec.health`,
`spec.tests`, `spec.permissions`, `spec.resources`. v0.1 picks the
smallest field set that keeps Modules 2–4 teachable; the owning
repository may promote any optional field to required in a later
version.

### A valid minimal capsule

The worked example from
[memo1 §3](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo1.md#3-worked-example-illustrative-not-valid-until-adopted-upstream),
restated at the identifier grammar adopted in memo2 §3 D3 and
published verbatim as
[`fixtures/valid/greeting.yaml`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/fixtures/valid/greeting.yaml):

```yaml
apiVersion: open-engineering.io/v1alpha1
kind: Capsule
metadata:
  name: greeting
  version: 0.1.0
spec:
  capability: oe.greeting
  inputs:
    value:
      type: string
      required: true
  outputs:
    greeting:
      type: string
  dependencies: []
```

## Capability identifier grammar (memo2 §3 D3)

A capability identifier is two or more dot-separated lower-case
segments; each segment starts with a lower-case ASCII letter and
otherwise contains lower-case ASCII letters, ASCII digits, or single
internal hyphens. The pattern, published in
[memo2 §3 D3](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo2.md#3-d3--capability-identifier-grammar-and-2-amendment)
and enforced by `capsule.schema.json`:

```
^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*)+$
```

Conforming examples (every conforming validator MUST accept):
`oe.greeting`, `github.issue.create`, `pico.state.set`.

Non-conforming examples (every conforming validator MUST reject):
`Greeting` (single segment, upper-case start), `oe..greeting` (empty
segment), `oe_greeting` (underscore not in the segment alphabet).

## Version compatibility constraints (memo2 §2 D2)

Every `metadata.version` MUST be a valid
[SemVer 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) string.
[memo2 §2 D2](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo2.md#2-d2--version-compatibility-rule)
defines three constraint forms a Pico may write in its
`spec.capabilities`:

| Written form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `oe.greeting` | Bare — any version matches. |
| `oe.greeting@0.1.0` | Caret — same major and version ≥ `0.1.0`; for `0.x`, same minor and patch ≥ `0`. |
| `oe.greeting@=0.1.0` | Exact — only `0.1.0` matches. |

The same section fixes the contract-level **breaking-change table**:

| Change in the capsule contract | Classification | Required bump |
|---|---|---|
| Remove a declared `spec.outputs` entry | Breaking | major |
| Add a new required `spec.inputs` entry | Breaking | major |
| Change the declared `type` of any input or output | Breaking | major |
| Change the `spec.capability` identifier | Breaking | major |
| Add an optional `spec.inputs` entry (no `required: true`) | Compatible | minor |
| Add a new `spec.outputs` entry | Compatible | minor |
| Documentation-only change | Compatible | patch |

## Contract, not implementation

A capsule document is a **contract**: it names a capability, declares
inputs and outputs by name and type, and pins a version — nothing
more. It carries no code and no runtime concern. The code that
satisfies the contract is a **capsule implementation**, which belongs
to `open-engineering-capsule/source` (the implementation org, memo2
§1 D1); the Academy does not fork or shadow it (memo23 §3.2). A Pico
composes a capability by writing a capability identifier into its
`spec.capabilities`; the reference validator resolves that identifier
to any installed capsule whose `spec.capability` matches and whose
`metadata.version` satisfies the stated constraint (memo2 §3 D3,
`fixtures/scenarios/resolve-greeting.yaml`). The contract is what
makes two independent implementations substitutable; everything
specific to one implementation stays inside that implementation.
